title: Plant and Animal Tissues
seo_title: Grade 10 Life Sciences: Plant and Animal Tissues Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 10 Life Sciences: Plant and animal tissues
standard_text: Tissues as groups of similar cells with a common function; plant tissues: meristematic, epidermis, parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma, xylem and phloem; animal tissues: epithelial, connective (including blood and bone), muscle and nerve tissue. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 10, Life Sciences: Plant and animal tissues)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): meristems, epidermis, parenchyma, xylem and phloem, and epithelial, connective, muscle and nerve tissue. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A tissue is a group of similar cells with the same function.
key_sub: Xylem carries water; phloem carries food.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plant tissues include meristems (dividing cells at tips), epidermis (protection), parenchyma (storage and photosynthesis), collenchyma and sclerenchyma (support), and the transport tissues xylem and phloem.

Animal tissues are of four kinds: epithelial tissue lines and covers surfaces; connective tissue (bone, cartilage, blood) supports and connects; muscle tissue contracts; nerve tissue carries impulses. Organs are made of several tissues working together.

Example

Which tissue carries water up a plant?

Dead, hollow vessels

Answer: xylem

Example

Which tissue type is blood?

It connects and transports.

Answer: connective tissue

Common mistakes

  • Thinking phloem carries water.
  • Thinking blood is not a tissue.
  • Mixing up tissues and organs.

faq.q: Why are xylem vessels hollow and strengthened with lignin?
faq.a: So that water can flow easily and the vessels do not collapse; lignin also supports the plant.

faq.q: What is the function of cilia on epithelial cells in the trachea?
faq.a: They sweep mucus and trapped dust away from the lungs.

items.q: Which cell has many chloroplasts, giving more light absorbed for photosynthesis?
items.e: Each specialised cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: Which cell has a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and a large Golgi body, giving many proteins made and packaged for secretion?
c: a pancreatic cell that secretes enzymes
items.e: Each specialised cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: Which feature is typical of a palisade mesophyll cell?
c: no nucleus and a biconcave shape
a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and a large Golgi body
items.e: A palisade mesophyll cell has many chloroplasts: more light absorbed for photosynthesis.

items.q: At which level of organisation is the circulatory system?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: At which level of organisation is the shoot system of a plant?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: Which cell has many mitochondria, giving more energy released by respiration for contraction?
c: a pancreatic cell that secretes enzymes
items.e: Each specialised cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: A palisade mesophyll cell has many chloroplasts. How does this help it?
c: more energy released by respiration for contraction
many proteins made and packaged for secretion
a larger surface area to absorb water and mineral salts
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: Where is blood found, or what does it do?
c: transporting substances round the body in a fluid matrix
the tip of the nose, the outer ear and between the vertebrae
items.e: Blood: transporting substances round the body in a fluid matrix.

items.q: A pancreatic cell that secretes enzymes has a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and a large Golgi body. How does this help it?
c: many proteins made and packaged for secretion
energy to swim to the egg
more energy released by respiration for contraction
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: Which cell has a thicker inner wall, giving a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma?
c: a pancreatic cell that secretes enzymes
items.e: Each specialised cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: just beneath the skin, as a support framework?
items.e: Areolar tissue: just beneath the skin, as a support framework.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs?
items.e: Squamous epithelium: the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.

items.q: Which feature is typical of a red blood cell?
c: a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and a large Golgi body
no nucleus and a biconcave shape
items.e: A red blood cell has no nucleus and a biconcave shape: more room for haemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen.

items.q: A sperm cell has a tail (flagellum) and many mitochondria. How does this help it?
c: a larger surface area to absorb water and mineral salts
more room for haemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen
energy to swim to the egg
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: At which level of organisation is a red blood cell?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: At which level of organisation is a root hair cell?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the wall of the heart?
items.e: Cardiac muscle: the wall of the heart.

items.q: A guard cell has a thicker inner wall. How does this help it?
c: energy to swim to the egg
more room for haemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen
many proteins made and packaged for secretion
a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: At which level of organisation is the heart?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: What is the main nitrogenous waste of a frog?
items.e: Tadpoles excrete ammonia.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as large empty cells in grass leaves that make them roll up in dry weather?
items.e: Bulliform cells: large empty cells in grass leaves that make them roll up in dry weather.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as specialised parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes?
items.e: Companion cells: specialised parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes.

items.q: What are annual rings?
c: the rings of the bark only
rings of spring wood and autumn wood formed each year
items.e: They are used to estimate a tree's age.

items.q: What is the periderm made of?
items.e: It replaces the epidermis in older stems.

items.q: What is endarch xylem?
c: protoxylem towards the centre and metaxylem towards the outside
items.e: Found in stems; roots are exarch.

items.q: Which description fits companion cells?
c: thin-walled living cells used for storage and photosynthesis
tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis
specialised parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes
openings in the bark for gas exchange
items.e: Companion cells: specialised parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as conducting water and minerals from roots?
items.e: Xylem: conducting water and minerals from roots.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss?
items.e: Cuticle: a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss.

items.q: What does the vascular cambium produce?
c: secondary xylem on the inside and secondary phloem on the outside
items.e: This causes growth in girth.

items.q: Which description fits palisade parenchyma?
c: tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis
openings in the bark for gas exchange
loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
items.e: Palisade parenchyma: tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis.

items.q: Which description fits phellem?
c: loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
cork, the dead outer layer of bark
thin-walled living cells used for storage and photosynthesis
items.e: Phellem: cork, the dead outer layer of bark.

items.q: What is sapwood?
c: the light-coloured outer wood that still conducts water
items.e: Also called alburnum.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis?
items.e: Palisade parenchyma: tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis.

items.q: Which description fits medullary rays?
c: thin-walled living cells used for storage and photosynthesis
parenchyma cells between the vascular bundles of a dicot stem
cells that open and close the stomatal pore
a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss
items.e: Medullary rays: parenchyma cells between the vascular bundles of a dicot stem.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as thin-walled living cells used for storage and photosynthesis?
items.e: Parenchyma: thin-walled living cells used for storage and photosynthesis.

items.q: Which description fits xylem?
c: loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems
dead cells with thick lignified walls that give mechanical support
conducting water and minerals from roots
items.e: Xylem: conducting water and minerals from roots.

items.q: Which description fits collenchyma?
c: dead cells with thick lignified walls that give mechanical support
openings in the bark for gas exchange
living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin
loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
items.e: Collenchyma: living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin.

items.q: Which elements of xylem are found mainly in angiosperms?
items.e: Gymnosperms lack vessels.

items.q: Which description fits sclerenchyma?
c: the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems
dead cells with thick lignified walls that give mechanical support
a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss
cork, the dead outer layer of bark
items.e: Sclerenchyma: dead cells with thick lignified walls that give mechanical support.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as cells that open and close the stomatal pore?
items.e: Guard cells: cells that open and close the stomatal pore.

items.q: Which description fits phellogen?
c: large empty cells in grass leaves that make them roll up in dry weather
cork, the dead outer layer of bark
the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex
the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems
items.e: Phellogen: the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex.

items.q: What is the outermost layer of the primary plant body?
items.e: It is covered by cuticle in shoots.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots?
items.e: Pericycle: the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf?
items.e: Spongy parenchyma: loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf.

items.q: Which description fits parenchyma?
c: the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots
dead cells with thick lignified walls that give mechanical support
the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots
thin-walled living cells used for storage and photosynthesis
items.e: Parenchyma: thin-walled living cells used for storage and photosynthesis.

items.q: Which description fits phloem?
c: living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin
tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis
cork, the dead outer layer of bark
items.e: Phloem: transporting food from leaves.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots?
items.e: Endodermis: the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots.

items.q: Which description fits cuticle?
c: parenchyma cells between the vascular bundles of a dicot stem
a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss
the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex
items.e: Cuticle: a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin?
items.e: Collenchyma: living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex?
items.e: Phellogen: the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as parenchyma cells between the vascular bundles of a dicot stem?
items.e: Medullary rays: parenchyma cells between the vascular bundles of a dicot stem.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems?
items.e: Hypodermis: the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems.

items.q: Which description fits bulliform cells?
c: large empty cells in grass leaves that make them roll up in dry weather
the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots
dead cells with thick lignified walls that give mechanical support
loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
items.e: Bulliform cells: large empty cells in grass leaves that make them roll up in dry weather.

items.q: Which description fits endodermis?
c: the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots
the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots
parenchyma cells between the vascular bundles of a dicot stem
tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis
items.e: Endodermis: the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots.

items.q: Which description fits spongy parenchyma?
c: loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
cork, the dead outer layer of bark
living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin
specialised parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes
items.e: Spongy parenchyma: loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf.

items.q: Which cells guard the stomata of grasses?
items.e: Dicots have bean-shaped guard cells.

items.q: Which description fits guard cells?
c: thin-walled living cells used for storage and photosynthesis
cells that open and close the stomatal pore
dead cells with thick lignified walls that give mechanical support
tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis
items.e: Guard cells: cells that open and close the stomatal pore.

items.q: What is a dorsiventral leaf?
c: a leaf with palisade on the upper side and spongy tissue below, as in dicots
a leaf with the same tissue on both sides
items.e: Isobilateral leaves (grasses) differ.

items.q: Which description fits pericycle?
c: the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots
loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
specialised parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes
the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex
items.e: Pericycle: the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as cork, the dead outer layer of bark?
items.e: Phellem: cork, the dead outer layer of bark.

items.q: Why is the frog called cold-blooded?
c: its body temperature changes with the environment (poikilothermic)
items.e: It goes into winter sleep (hibernation).

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the mouth and pharynx?
items.e: Compound epithelium: the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the mouth and pharynx.

items.q: Which glands release secretions through ducts?
items.e: e.g. salivary glands and mucus glands.

items.q: Which junctions stop substances from leaking across a tissue?
items.e: Gap junctions let ions and small molecules pass between cells.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone?
items.e: Tendon: connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone.

items.q: Where is smooth muscle found, or what does it do?
c: the wall of the stomach and intestine
the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs
items.e: Smooth muscle: the wall of the stomach and intestine.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: connecting a bone to another bone?
items.e: Ligament: connecting a bone to another bone.

items.q: Which muscle is involuntary and striated?
items.e: It has intercalated discs.

items.q: Where is adipose tissue found, or what does it do?
c: the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons
the wall of the stomach and intestine
the tip of the nose, the outer ear and between the vertebrae
items.e: Adipose tissue: storing fat below the skin.

items.q: Which muscle is voluntary and striated?
items.e: It is attached to bones.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons?
items.e: Cuboidal epithelium: the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the lining of the stomach and intestine, with tall cells?
items.e: Columnar epithelium: the lining of the stomach and intestine, with tall cells.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the bronchioles and fallopian tubes?
items.e: Ciliated epithelium: the bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

items.q: Where is columnar epithelium found, or what does it do?
c: the tip of the nose, the outer ear and between the vertebrae
the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the mouth and pharynx
the lining of the stomach and intestine, with tall cells
items.e: Columnar epithelium: the lining of the stomach and intestine, with tall cells.

items.q: Which connective tissue has a fluid matrix?
items.e: Plasma is its matrix.

items.q: Where is cuboidal epithelium found, or what does it do?
c: just beneath the skin, as a support framework
the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons
the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs
connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
items.e: Cuboidal epithelium: the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: storing fat below the skin?
items.e: Adipose tissue: storing fat below the skin.

items.q: Where is ligament found, or what does it do?
c: transporting substances round the body in a fluid matrix
connecting a bone to another bone
connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
items.e: Ligament: connecting a bone to another bone.

items.q: What do gap junctions do?
c: they connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells for rapid transfer of ions and small molecules
items.e: Found in cardiac muscle.

items.q: Where is compound epithelium found, or what does it do?
c: just beneath the skin, as a support framework
the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the mouth and pharynx
items.e: Compound epithelium: the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the mouth and pharynx.

items.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
c: tissue → cell → organ → organ system → organism
cell → organ → tissue → organ system → organism
cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
cell → tissue → organ system → organ → organism
items.e: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form systems.

items.q: Which organ system does the spinal cord belong to?
items.e: The spinal cord is part of the nervous system.

items.q: Which level of organisation is an oak tree?
items.e: An oak tree is an organism.

items.q: Which organ system does the trachea belong to?
items.e: The trachea is part of the respiratory system.

items.q: Which level of organisation is the digestive system?
items.e: The digestive system is an organ system.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for pulling your hand away from a hot stove?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

items.q: How many chambers does a frog's heart have?
c: three: two atria and one ventricle
items.e: There is also a sinus venosus and conus arteriosus.

items.q: How does a frog breathe in water?
c: it does not breathe in water
items.e: On land it also uses its lungs and buccal cavity.

items.q: What level comes right after tissue (going from small to large)?
items.e: tissue → organ.

items.q: Lindiwe asks: what is the main job of the nervous system?
c: It supports the body and protects organs.
It collects information and sends messages that control the body.
It breaks food down into nutrients the body can use.
It moves the body by pulling on bones.
items.e: The nervous system collects information and sends messages that control the body.

items.q: Which level of organisation is xylem?
items.e: Xylem is a tissue.

items.q: Which organ system does the thyroid gland belong to?
items.e: The thyroid gland is part of the endocrine system.

items.q: Aisha reads about a body system that collects information and sends messages that control the body. Which system is it?
items.e: The nervous system collects information and sends messages that control the body.

items.q: Where is tendon found, or what does it do?
c: connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
the wall of the stomach and intestine
the tip of the nose, the outer ear and between the vertebrae
the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the mouth and pharynx
items.e: Tendon: connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone.

items.q: Where is cardiac muscle found, or what does it do?
c: connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
items.e: Cardiac muscle: the wall of the heart.

items.q: Which organ system does the kidneys belong to?
items.e: The kidneys is part of the excretory (urinary) system.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for removing wastes from the blood?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

items.q: Which level of organisation is a lung?
items.e: A lung is an organ.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for breathing faster when you run?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

items.q: Which organ system does the pancreas (making insulin) belong to?
items.e: The pancreas (making insulin) is part of the endocrine system.
